newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish borrowing costs lower in EMU - debt office.
newsitem.headline: Swedish borrowing costs lower in EMU - debt office.

text.p: Sweden's National Debt Office said on Monday that the costs of state borrowing would be lower if Sweden joined the European economic and monetary union (EMU).
The debt office said an official report on EMU commissioned by the government had underestimated the costs of delayed participation in monetary union.
"There are overwhelming reasons to believe that costs of state borrowing would be lower if Sweden joined EMU," the debt office said in a statement.
The debt office said upward pressure on interest rates would occur if Sweden did not join.
The debt office said borrowing in Euro instead of Swedish crown would mean a larger investment base for Swedish borrowers.

"The office sees major weaknesses in a long term (actual or expected) resistance to joining EMU. In that approach lies a risk that access to Swedish crowns will be judged as less interesting for both domestic and foreign investors and that the government securities market would deteriorate. This would increase the state's borrowing costs," the debt office said. -- Simon Haydon, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1004 .
